title: Bouncers at Small's Paradise, Connie's Inn and the Savoy
summary: The big clubs were protected by strong-arm men, some ex-prizefighters, who kept the crowds in line and quietly removed troublemakers.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: How about, say, Mr. Small and Mr. Wilkin's ability to maintain these clubs. They managed all right, apparently.

Oh yeah. Small's Paradise was right on the same level as the Cotton Club was on. They had people in those clubs -- It wasn't no headache for them. They had people that were taking care of the crowd. They had, like, strong-armed guys. Bouncers back there. They had bouncers. They had people that people respected. Fools wouldn't go down there and want to start -- they know better to go in the -- You don't go into Small's Paradise. You

wouldn't go into Connie's Inn and start nothing, you know. Those clubs were well protected by people that knew how to protect people. And they tell you to come and bring your family, bring -- come hear you, but protect you. They don't care how many people down there. And nobody going to get out of line. That club would be packed. You couldn't go to another table and start no argument with somebody. First think you know, three guys got you and you'll be out of there. There's quite a few that disappeared -- no argument (inaudible). And don't worry about it. When you go outside, ain't nobody going to bother you because they protect the inside. Outside the club they protect you, because they got people all -- They had bouncers downstairs -- on a weekend the club is packed. Now, you're going to have a lot of guys that wanna get out of line, trying to mess at somebody's table, something like that. But no, no. There was respect at

that place. like Savoy. You know the Savoy Ballroom? They had ex-prizefighters. Now you wouldn't believe this. They had guys who were ex-prizefighters, strong-arm guys dressed in tuxedos. They didn't make you (inaudible) or do anything to you. When you come up here, they'll tell you, "Now look, behave yourself. Don't come here to take out your grievance on nobody. You got a disagreement with somebody, take it outside." Or else they're going to take you down to the basement. Don't start nothing there! So the Savoy Ballroom was ran just like a hotel, or something like this. You know, you didn't come up there to start no argument. Very few fights we had in the ballroom. If we did, it was over just like that. Because they had guys standing up levels. They could look over and see the crowd. One will be at the end, the east. One will be at the north end, south end.
